sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球供应链制造母港、跨境电商货源地与外资合规准入市场

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Chartering and Operation of Offshore Platform Support Ships

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China (HKSAR)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Common Law in Hong Kong within PRC civil law sovereign framework)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Mainland and Hong Kong Closer Economic Partnership Arrangement (CEPA) and its Agreement on Trade in Services (signed 28 November 2015, as amended)
Investment Agreement between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (signed 28 June 2017, effective 1 January 2018)

Arrangement between the Mainland of China and the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with respect to Taxes on Income (signed 21 August 2006, as amended by the Second Protocol)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 revision, effective 1 January 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information (Order No. 3 [2024] of the People's Bank of China and the State Administration for Market Regulation, effective 1 November 2024); Hong Kong Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance (Cap. 615); Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap. 37); Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622); Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Certificate of Registration of the Foreign-Invested Partnership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry (or State Administration for Market Regulation for Mainland China FIP registration)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path (mutually exclusive with consular legalization): issue the public certificate; affix an Apostille through the High Court of Hong Kong (for HK public documents) or through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the PRC / provincial foreign affairs office after Chinese notarization (for Mainland China public documents); do not chain consular legalization after Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Continuing Registration or Compliance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Hong Kong Companies Registry and Inland Revenue Department Business Registration Office (or SAMR as applicable)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path only: for HK-issued certificates, obtain a certified copy and affix Apostille by the High Court of Hong Kong; for PRC-issued certificates, notarize the certificate with a Chinese notary office and then apostille through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs / provincial foreign affairs office. Consular legalization is not added. If the document originates in a non-Hague member state, substitute consular legalization in place of Apostille, never sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution / Power of Attorney authorizing formation, name clearance, UBO filing, and bank onboarding
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Parent entity board of directors (China-side investor) and authorized notarial authorities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For a Mainland China issuer: notarization by a competent Chinese notary office, followed by Apostille by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the PRC or its entrusted provincial foreign affairs office; the Apostille-certified document is then submitted to Hong Kong authorities and banks. Consular legalization is not required and must not be layered onto the Apostille. A non-Hague issuing state follows only the consular legalization route.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Limited Partnership Agreement / Constituent Deed
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding partners and corporate services provider (registered agent) authorized under the constitutive documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path where the signatories are in Hong Kong: notarize signatures before a Hong Kong notary public and obtain an Apostille from the High Court of Hong Kong; where executed in Mainland China: notarize before a Chinese notary office and apostille through the PRC Ministry of Foreign Affairs / provincial foreign affairs office. Consular legalization is a separate parallel route for non-Apostille states and is never combined with Apostille.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter (investor creditworthiness, banking relationship, and facility history)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Investor's qualifying bank in China, Hong Kong, or the investor's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Private bank document route: issue on bank letterhead and sign by the branch officer; notarize the officer's signature; if the issuing jurisdiction is a Hague Apostille member, affix the Apostille from the designated competent authority; if the issuing jurisdiction is not a Hague Apostille member, use consular legalization only. The two authentication paths are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening before onboarding and at least every 90 days for all partners, directors, authorized signatories, ultimate beneficial owners, commercial counterparties, charterers, sub-charterers, vessel managers, and brokers against: OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List; UN Security Council Consolidated List; EU and UK consolidated financial sanctions targets; Chinese domestic sanctions and export-control lists maintained by MOFCOM, MIIT, and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs; Hong Kong sanction regimes under the United Nations Sanctions Ordinance (Cap. 537) and the Regulating Other Risks in Financial Sector (Sanctions) Ordinance (Cap. 675); and politically exposed person databases covering family members and known close associates. Enhanced due diligence is triggered by PEP status, high-risk maritime jurisdictions, shell-company counterparties, unusual charter routes, complex ownership chains, and any crypto exposure. Source of wealth and source of funds must be documented; any hit or unexplained discrepancy must be escalated to the Anti-Money Laundering Reporting Officer before formation or bank account opening.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Hong Kong Companies Registry Integrated Companies Registry Information System (ICRIS) Cyber Search Centre and e-Registry Name Check facility; for Mainland China FIP name approval, the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System / online name pre-registration portal.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Hong Kong permits an English name and, optionally, a Chinese name expressed in Traditional Chinese characters; a Chinese name that is a phonetic transliteration of the English name must not mislead as to the nature and scope of the business. For a Mainland China FIP, the Chinese name must be in Simplified Chinese characters and must follow the mandatory four-tier naming

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 37) of the Laws of Hong Kong, particularly sections 4 (Registration), 5 (Effect of Registration), and 7 (Particulars to be Registered); Business Registration Ordinance (Cap. 310) sections 6 and 9; Companies Ordinance (Cap. 622) Part 11 (Non-Hong Kong Companies) as applicable to foreign-invested partnerships; and the Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 38) for general partnership principles.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR (for limited partnership registration) and Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department (for business registration certificate).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Form LP1 (Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership) and Form IRBR1 (Application for Business Registration)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Hong Kong law imposes no minimum paid-up capital requirement for limited partnerships. Capital contributions are determined by the partnership agreement and may be in cash, property, or services. No escrow or blocked account is mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER AND MANAGEMENT COMMITTEE OF [FIP NAME] (THE 'PARTNERSHIP') ADOPTED BY WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF A MEETING ON [DATE]

WHEREAS the Partnership is a foreign-invested limited partnership duly organized under the Limited Partnership Ordinance (Cap. 37) of Hong Kong, with its principal place of business at [Registered Office Address];

WHEREAS the Partnership Agreement dated [Date] authorizes the General Partner to manage the affairs of the Partnership and to adopt resolutions by written consent without a formal meeting;

NOW, THEREFORE, IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:

1. CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION AND CONTRIBUTIONS: That the initial capital contributions of the partners, as set forth in Schedule A of the Partnership Agreement, are hereby ratified and accepted. The General Partner is authorized to issue capital calls to the limited partners in accordance with the agreed contribution schedule, and to deposit all such funds into the Partnership's designated bank account. No partner shall have the right to withdraw capital except as expressly permitted by the Partnership Agreement and applicable law.

2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: That the following banks are hereby designated as the Partnership's primary banking institutions: [Bank Name] and [Bank Name]. The General Partner, together with any two authorized signatories (as listed in the Partnership's mandate), are jointly and severally authorized to open, operate, and manage all bank accounts, including but not limited to current accounts, savings accounts, and foreign currency accounts. The authorized signatories shall have the power to execute all banking documents, endorse checks, initiate wire transfers, and enter into any banking agreements on behalf of the Partnership. This authorization shall remain in full force until revoked by a subsequent resolution.

3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: That the registered office of the Partnership shall be situated at [Full Address in Hong Kong], which is a physical address within Hong Kong SAR. The General Partner is directed to file the necessary notice of change of registered office with the Companies Registry, if applicable, and to ensure that all statutory records and registers are maintained at this address. The registered office shall be open to the public during normal business hours for inspection of the Partnership's register of partners and other statutory documents.

4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: That the following individuals are hereby appointed to the following offices of the Partnership: (a) [Name] as General Partner and Chief Executive Officer, with full authority to manage the day-to-day operations; (b) [Name] as Compliance Officer, responsible for ensuring adherence to all applicable laws, including anti-money laundering and sanctions regulations; (c) [Name] as Company Secretary (if applicable), to maintain statutory records and file all required returns; and (d) [Name] as Chief Financial Officer, with authority over financial reporting and tax compliance. Each officer shall serve until resignation, removal, or successor appointment.

5. GENERAL AUTHORIZATION: That the General Partner and each officer are hereby authorized to execute, deliver, and file all documents, instruments, and certificates necessary to effectuate the foregoing resolutions, including but not limited to contracts, leases, licenses, and regulatory filings. Any such execution shall be binding upon the Partnership.

6. EFFECTIVE DATE: This resolution shall be effective as of the date of adoption and shall be recorded in the Partnership's minute book.

ADOPTED by the General Partner and the Management Committee on the date first written above.

[Signature of General Partner]
[Name and Title]

[Signature of Witness]
[Name and Title]

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR (online via e-Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a name search on the Companies Registry's Cyber Search Centre to ensure the proposed partnership name is not identical to or confusingly similar to an existing entity. If the name is available, file an application for name reservation using Form NNC1 (for companies) or the equivalent for limited partnerships, which is not formally required but recommended. For limited partnerships, the name must end with 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.'. Submit the application online or in person, pay the prescribed fee (HK$1,720 for registration, but name reservation is free if done during registration). The registry will issue a name reservation certificate valid for 3 months. If the name is rejected, select an alternative and resubmit.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name (in English and Chinese if desired)
Identification documents of all partners (passport or HKID)
Proof of address of each partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected due to similarity, the applicant may file a formal objection with the Companies Registry within 14 days, providing evidence of prior use or consent from the existing entity. Alternatively, amend the name and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Companies Registry, Hong Kong SAR (Registry of Limited Partnerships)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and sign Form LP1 (Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership) in duplicate. The form must include the partnership name, nature of business, principal place of business, names and addresses of all general and limited partners, and the amount of capital contributed by each limited partner. Attach a certified copy of the partnership agreement (if any) and the name reservation certificate. Submit the form and supporting documents to the Companies Registry either in person at the counter or by post. Pay the registration fee of HK$1,720 (approx. USD 220) plus any additional levy. The registry will review the application for completeness and compliance with the Limited Partnership Ordinance. Upon approval, the registry will issue a Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership. This certificate is conclusive evidence of compliance with registration requirements.
required_dossiers: Proof of principal place of business (e.g., tenancy agreement)
Consent to act as general partner (if not a natural person)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, the registry will issue a notice specifying deficiencies. The applicant must respond within 14 days with corrections or additional documents. If the application is suspended, the applicant may appeal to the Registrar within 21 days, providing a written explanation and supporting evidence. If the issue is not resolved, the applicant may re-file after rectifying the defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department (IRD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of the commencement of business, apply for a Business Registration Certificate using Form IRBR1. The application must be submitted to the Business Registration Office, either online via the eTAX system or in person. Provide the partnership's registration certificate, the partnership agreement, and the principal place of business address. The fee is HK$2,000 per year (or HK$250 for a one-year certificate if the business is small). The IRD will issue a Business Registration Certificate and a Business Registration Fee Receipt. This certificate must be displayed prominently at the place of business. The BRC is renewable annually.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected, the IRD will provide reasons. The applicant may appeal to the Commissioner of Inland Revenue within 1 month, submitting additional evidence. If the rejection is due to incomplete information, the applicant may resubmit the form with the missing details. If the business is not yet operational, the applicant may apply for a 'non-active' status, but must still obtain the BRC.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Opening and Statutory Officer Appointments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial banks in Hong Kong (e.g., HSBC, Standard Chartered) and the Partnership's own governance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the BRC, open a corporate bank account in the partnership's name. Provide the bank with the Certificate of Registration, BRC, partnership agreement, and identification of all authorized signatories. The bank will conduct due diligence, including beneficial ownership checks and source of funds verification. Simultaneously, formally appoint the statutory officers (General Partner, Compliance Officer, Company Secretary, CFO) by passing a written resolution as per the pro-forma resolution. Ensure that the officers' appointments are recorded in the partnership's minute book and that any required filings with the Companies Registry (e.g., appointment of a company secretary if the partnership is a company) are made. For a limited partnership, no filing of officer appointments is required, but the partnership agreement should be updated.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Registration of Limited Partnership
Board resolution appointing officers (as per pro-forma)
Identification and proof of address of all signatories
Bank's account opening forms and due diligence questionnaires
Reference letters from existing banks (if required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the account application, the partnership may apply to another bank or provide additional documentation to address the bank's concerns. If the bank requests further information, respond promptly. If the appointment of officers is challenged, the partnership may amend the resolution and re-file. For any regulatory queries, the partnership may seek legal advice and respond within the specified timeframe.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Marine Department, Hong Kong SAR (for vessel licensing and maritime safety) and the Environmental Protection Department (EPD) for environmental compliance
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Vessel Operating Licence (under the Shipping and Port Control Ordinance, Cap. 313) and a Marine Department Licence for Chartering of Offshore Support Vessels

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Department (EPD), Hong Kong SAR
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Registration (Category 2) – not a full EIA report, but requires registration and compliance with the Air Pollution Control Ordinance (Cap. 311) and the Water Pollution Control Ordinance (Cap. 358).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Vessels must comply with the Merchant Shipping (Prevention of Air Pollution) Regulation (Cap. 413) which limits sulphur content in marine fuel to 0.5% m/m (global standard) and nitrogen oxide emissions to Tier II standards. Wastewater discharges must meet the standards under the Water Pollution Control Ordinance, with a maximum biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) of 20 mg/L and suspended solids of 30 mg/L for treated effluent. Hazardous waste handling must comply with the Waste Disposal Ordinance (Cap. 354), including proper storage, labeling, and disposal through licensed contractors. Vessels must also adhere to the International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships (MARPOL) Annexes I-VI.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification is required from the Fire Services Department (FSD) for any onshore facilities, including offices and warehouses. For vessels, the Marine Department issues a Certificate of Survey and a Safety Management Certificate under the International Safety Management (ISM) Code. Occupational safety on vessels is governed by the Merchant Shipping (Safety) Ordinance (Cap. 369) and the Occupational Safety and Health Ordinance (Cap. 509). The vessel must undergo a structural load inspection and obtain a Load Line Certificate. Additionally, a Port Facility Security Plan must be approved by the Marine Department under the International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; online registration and compliance portal: National Electronic Tax Administration (e-Tax platform) accessible at the provincial STA electronic tax bureau websites under the unified China Tax electronic portal; tax affairs handled through the Electronic Tax Bureau (Electronic Tax Administration) system with the Unified Social Credit Code as the master data key.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP) established by Hong Kong and other non-resident partners, the mandatory sequence is: (1) Complete SAMR (State Administration for Market Regulation) enterprise name approval and business license registration; the business license contains the 18-character Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which by operation of law constitutes the FIP's Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT registration number; (2) Foreign partners must supply notarized, apostilled/legalized identity or incorporation documents with certified Chinese translation - for Hong Kong partners, a Hong Kong Certificate of Incorporation and current Business Registration Certificate; (3) Within 30 calendar days of receiving the business license, complete the initial tax registration (including income tax, VAT, withholding, city maintenance and construction tax, education surcharge) at the competent local STA branch of the FIP's registered address using the e-Tax portal or in-person counter; (4) Complete the FIP's tax registration information report, including partnership agreement allocation ratios, partners' identities and residential status; (5) Enroll for the fully digitalized electronic invoice system and tax control device authorization; (6) If the FIP will engage in vessel chartering subject to water transport licensing by the Ministry of Transport, the tax registration file must attach the corresponding shipping business license (Ship Operating Permit or Non-Vessel Operating Common Carrier endorsement as applicable).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - The FIP is fiscally transparent for China Enterprise Income Tax: the partnership itself is not a taxpayer; profits are allocated to partners pursuant to the partnership agreement and taxed in the hands of the partners; non-resident partners are taxed only on China-source income under the territorial scope principle, and HK resident partners may claim offshore credit relief under the China-Hong Kong comprehensive double tax arrangement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None - China has no check-the-box entity classification election or hybrid mismatch election analogous to the U.S. or OECD regimes; the pass-through transparency of an FIP is mandatory under the Measures for the Administration of Foreign-Invested Partnerships. Available elections limited to: (a) VAT status election between small-scale taxpayer simplified method (3% levy rate, no input credit) and general taxpayer method (standard rate with input VAT credit) where annual taxable turnover is below RMB 5,000,000; (b) partnership profit/loss allocation ratios as stipulated in the partnership agreement, subject to arm's length substance requirements; (c) election to apply deemed expense methodology for non-resident partner withholding in certain cross-border scenarios as prescribed by STA.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) - China's VAT under the Provisional VAT Regulations and Cai Shui [2016] No. 36 Notice, administered by the STA; for offshore vessel chartering with crew (wet charter), the service is classified as water transport at the 9% rate; for bareboat/dry charter without crew it is classified as tangible movable property leasing at the 13% rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VAT registration is compulsory for every entity obtaining a business license regardless of turnover; the Unified Social Credit Code is the VAT registration number. Mandatory general taxpayer status applies when annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000; below this threshold the FIP may elect small-scale taxpayer status at the 3% simplified levy rate, subject to current preferential reductions and the monthly small-scale exemption policy.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China has mandated the fully digitalized electronic invoice (Digital e-Invoice) system nationwide, replacing paper VAT invoices; every invoice must be issued through the National Electronic Tax Administration platform with real-time upload to the Golden Tax System Phase IV (anti-fraud tax control infrastructure); invoices carry a unique 20-digit electronic invoice number and encrypted QR code / digital anti-fraud stamp; no fiscal clearance stamping by a clearance authority is required for issuance, but all invoice data is subject to near-real-time risk screening by the STA; tax control devices remain required for taxpayers that still issue paper special VAT invoices.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Cai Shui [2016] No. 36 and the STA export VAT measures, the zero rate (0% VAT with full input credit and refund) applies to: (a) international water transport services engaging vessels to carry passengers or cargo from a port in China customs territory to a port outside China customs territory; and (b) cross-border services supplied to overseas entities and wholly consumed outside China, including the chartering and operation of offshore platform support vessels hired by non-resident oil and gas contractors for voyages and station-keeping exclusively outside China customs territory. If the chartered vessel performs any part of the contract within Chinese territorial waters or is used by a domestic operating company in China's continental shelf operations, the service is taxable at the standard (9%) rate and zero-rating is unavailable. The FIP must establish a complete paper trail demonstrating the offshore destination of the service, the non-resident party contracting the charter, and the receipt of foreign currency consideration.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Customs export bill / export customs clearance document) evidencing the physical departure or deemed export of the vessel or vessel-related supplies from China customs territory, where goods or spares are involved
Bill of Lading (or sea waybill / charter party receipt) showing carriage from a China port to a foreign destination or offshore installation outside China customs territory
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) issued by a designated Chinese foreign exchange bank evidencing the receipt and conversion of foreign currency charter hire from the non-resident charterer
Cross-border vessel charter agreement (English/Chinese bilingual) specifying the charter party, offshore service area, and non-resident counterparty
Commercial invoice and packing list (bilingual) together with the fully digitalized VAT invoice annotated as zero-rated export
Vessel delivery / redelivery certificates, voyage reports and satellite AIS logs proving the service was performed outside China customs territory

Service Trade Foreign Exchange Verification Notice and registration records from the SAFE (State Administration of Foreign Exchange) digital monitoring system confirming the foreign exchange receipt is matched to the declared export service
Ship Operation License or approved Vessel Operation Permit evidencing the legal capacity for international offshore marine charter during the VAT refund filing period
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA, China Customs and SAFE maintain a joint export audit framework; claimed zero-rated refunds are examined against customs declarations, FX repatriation records and service trade verification. Where zero-rating is found improper: the refund and input VAT credits are clawed back with late-payment interest; a penalty of 50% to 500% of the tax amount is imposed under Article 63 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law for evasion by false export declarations; suppliers committing fraudulent export VAT refund are barred from export tax rebate qualification for a period, blacklisted in the Untrustworthy Taxpayers list and referred for criminal prosecution under Article 204 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China for defrauding export tax refunds, punishable by up to life imprisonment and confiscation in aggravated cases; the retrospective clawback period is 5 years from the end of the taxable year, extended to 10 years where fraud is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) through the State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The People's Republic of China maintains a managed foreign exchange regime with full current-account convertibility for lawful trade and service transactions, but a strictly controlled capital account. RMB is fully convertible under the current account for remitting freight, charter hire, insurance premiums, and other genuine maritime operational expenses. Capital account transactions, including inbound equity or partnership capital contributions from Hong Kong into a Chinese Foreign-Invested Partnership (FIP), require SAFE registration, a foreign exchange capital account, and post-receipt capital verification by a qualified Chinese accounting firm. Profit and dividend remittances from the FIP to its Hong Kong partners are permitted only after annual audits, corporate income tax settlement by the FIP in the Chinese mainland (or through its partners as pass-through if so classified), and the presentation of a completed 'Service Trade & Profit/Remittance Certificate' from the local SAFE branch or via the bank's digital compliance portal. No mandatory surrender or forced conversion ratio currently applies to export or service receipts, but all foreign currency earnings from offshore vessel charters and maritime support services must be repatriated into China within 180 days after the relevant customs declaration or service completion date. Repatriated dollars may be retained in a designated foreign exchange settlement account or converted to RMB at the market exchange rate. The FIP must also lodge a 'Payment/Delivery Verification' record with SAFE within 30 days of any remittance and maintain underlying charter party contracts, invoices, and operational logs as audit evidence. In essence, convertibility is available for genuine working capital and service flows, while equity, liquidity, and leverage-related capital movements are individually screened by SAFE and the reporting licensed commercial bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under SAFE regulations, export and service proceeds must be repatriated into China within 180 days from the export declaration or service completion date. There is no statutorily mandated conversion ratio; the FIP may hold the foreign currency in an approved foreign exchange settlement account or convert all or part of it into RMB at prevailing rate, but each transaction must be supported by the underlying offshore vessel chartering agreement, commercial invoices, and a valid marine logistics service contract.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (SAFE-verified foreign exchange capital account for inbound FDI and partnership contribution)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Basic Operational Currency Account (RMB current account and foreign exchange settlement account)
FID Escrow Repatriation Reserve Account (dual-currency operating account with cross-border clearing capability)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Offshore digital EMIs are legally barred from opening domestic RMB settlement accounts or serving as a formal depository bank for a Chinese-registered Foreign-Invested Partnership. The PBOC and SAFE only license approved payment institutions for cross-border intermediary settlement, but such institutions do not carry the legal status of banks and cannot provide capital verification, FX conversion certificates, or SAFE-registered fiduciary accounts for a China FIP. The FIP must maintain its primary treasury relationship with a licensed domestic commercial bank, while a fintech EMI may be used at best as a niche overlay for small incidental payments, subject to full PBOC scrutiny and without replacing the bank account structure.

stage_4.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The statutory general partner or an expressly authorized senior manager of the FIP must appear physically in-branch to satisfy PBOC and SAFE face-to-face compliance. Remote consular proxy opening of the initial RMB basic account or foreign exchange capital account is not permitted. If a non-resident general partner cannot travel, the bank may accept a notarized and legalized blanket power of attorney appointing a local managing partner or employee, provided that the original ID of that appointee is presented alongside the full statutory filing documents from the Mainland Market Supervision Administration and the HK parent partner's certified corporate registry records. In-person biographical and beneficial owner interviews are mandatory at account opening and upon any change of control.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business Registration Certificate renewal under the Business Registration Ordinance (Cap 310)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Business Registration Office, Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the expiry date stated on the current Business Registration Certificate; the Inland Revenue Department issues a renewal demand approximately one month before expiry, and payment is due by the demand due date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal is an offence; a late-payment penalty of HK$300 may be imposed under Cap 310, and failure to hold a valid certificate exposes the partnership to a maximum fine of HK$5,000 and six months' imprisonment on first conviction; continued default may result in administrative cancellation of the business registration record and prohibition on obtaining an Inland Revenue certificate of compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profits Tax Return - Partnership (Form BIR52) for each year of assessment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department (Profits Tax Unit), Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due within one month from the date of issue stated on the BIR52 form; the form is normally issued on 1 April of the following year of assessment, and a later extension may be granted when the partnership is represented by a Hong Kong tax representative
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing is prosecuted in the District Court; a starting penalty of HK$1,200 may be imposed and increased to HK$3,000 for continued non-compliance; the Inland Revenue may raise an estimated profits assessment without appeal rights, and a 10% additional tax under section 82A of the Inland Revenue Ordinance may be charged on understatements; repeat offenders may face HK$50,000 plus an additional 100% assessment.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Employer's Annual Return (Form BIR56A) for employees or marine crew, and Employer's Return of Remuneration and Pensions (Form BIR56B), if the partnership employs staff
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Inland Revenue Department, Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month from the issue date on the return; returns are normally issued in early April for the preceding year of assessment ending 31 March
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may result in a fine of HK$10,000 and a further daily default fine of HK$50; knowingly failing to comply may lead to prosecution, additional tax under section 80 of the Inland Revenue Ordinance, and loss of tax deductions for the related remuneration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Notice of Change in Limited Partnership (Form LP2) covering changes to partners, capital contributions, profit sharing ratios, name, or registered principal place of business
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies (Limited Partnerships Registry), Hong Kong SAR
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 days after any change in the constitution of the limited partnership; this is a recurring statutory event rather than an annual anniversary filing, and it is triggered on each transfer of a partner's interest
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Every general partner knowingly failing to file may be liable for a fine of HK$5,000, and the Registrar may refuse to register the change; continuous default may cause the limited partnership's registration to be flagged for strike-off from the Limited Partnerships Register, exposing general partners to unlimited liability for partnership obligations arising after default.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Hong Kong law, an unincorporated limited partnership under the Limited Partnerships Ordinance (Cap 37) has no statutory audit obligation solely by reason of size, turnover, or headcount. A mandatory certified CPA audit is legally triggered only when the partnership holds an SFC-regulated activity licence under the Securities and Futures Ordinance, is a licensed trust or company service provider under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance, is registered as a Limited Partnership Fund under Cap 637 whose fund documents require audited accounts, or is required under a vessel finance facility or charterer agreement. For Hong Kong private companies, by analogy, a mandatory statutory audit is triggered when the company is not a small private company, meaning it fails to satisfy at least two of three criteria: annual total revenue not exceeding HK$100 million, total assets not exceeding HK$100 million, and headcount not exceeding 100 employees. For this offshore platform support vessel chartering partnership, no compulsory size-based audit arises under Cap 622 unless the partnership is separately constituted as a company or a Hong Kong-registered vessel operating entity is subject to Marine Department licensing conditions requiring audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Hong Kong Financial Reporting Standards (HKFRS) as issued by the Hong Kong Institute of Certified Public Accountants, which are aligned with IFRS; eligible private entities may adopt HKFRS for Private Entities. For a partnership engaged in offshore supply vessel leasing, the financial statements must apply HKFRS 16 / IFRS 16 for charter and lease contracts, HKFRS 15 for revenue recognition, and HKAS 1 for presentation, and must be reconciled to the Inland Revenue Ordinance profits tax computation where amounts are adjusted for tax reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO confirmation is filed on the public registers for a Hong Kong limited partnership. The partnership must instead maintain a current internal beneficial-ownership and partner-interest record at its registered office and verify each partner's identity under AML record-keeping duties where the partnership falls within the DNFBP regime or is a trust and company service provider. On any transfer, assignment, or increase of a limited partner's interest, the partnership must lodge Form LP2 with the Registrar of Companies within 7 days and update the internal UBO schedule at the registered office; this 7-day statutory window supersedes the 30-day corporate shareholding filing window applicable to Hong Kong companies under the Companies Ordinance significant controllers regime.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (equivalent in a partnership: Register of Limited Partners with capital contributions, profit-share percentages, and transfer history)
Register of Directors (equivalent in a partnership: Register of General Partners with identity, authority, and unlimited liability acknowledgement)
Register of Charges and Mortgages over the partnership's vessel fleet, charter rights, and marine assets
Statutory Minute Book containing partner resolutions, consents, and management committee minutes

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15% (standard Hong Kong profits tax rate for unincorporated partnerships under the two-tiered regime: 7.5% on the first HK$2,000,000 of assessable profits and 15% on the remainder; the corporate rate would be 16.5% if the vehicle were a corporation)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial source exemption for charter profits wholly derived outside Hong Kong (offshore claim); Inland Revenue (Amendment) (Ship Leasing) Ordinance 2023 concession: 0% profits tax on qualifying ship leasing profits of a qualifying ship lessor and 8.25% on qualifying ship leasing management, subject to Hong Kong core income-generating activities, minimum staffing and expense conditions; no capital gains tax; no GST/VAT on charter hire; statutory depreciation allowances for vessel acquisition under IRO s.16F; treaty relief under the PRC-Hong Kong Double Taxation Arrangement at 7% for interest and 5% for royalties

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profits Tax Return - Form BIR52 (Partnership Return, i.e., persons other than corporations), filed electronically through the Inland Revenue Department (IRD) eTAX portal with the supporting partnership capital, profit-sharing schedule and audited financial statements
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return must be filed within 1 month of the issue date; for accounting periods ending 31 December, the IRD generally issues BIR52 on 1 April of the following year with a statutory due date of 2 May, and where the partnership is represented by a Hong Kong tax representative the extended eTAX filing deadline is typically mid-August of the year of assessment

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business name of the Foreign-Invested Partnership, Business Registration (BR) number, principal place of business in Hong Kong, and the full names, addresses, tax identification numbers and profit-share ratios of all partners, including non-resident partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Each non-resident partner (e.g., a PRC corporate investor) must be declared with its country of tax residence and its exact partnership profit-share percentage; the partnership must appoint a Hong Kong resident tax representative or authorised agent; the IRD will raise a separate assessment on each non-resident partner under IRO s.22 and s.23, and Form IR1249 Individual/Partner Return Schedule will be issued; omission of a controlling PRC partner constitutes an incorrect return and may trigger the IRD offshore-claim audit programme

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Principal business activity code (HKPSIC / ISIC) and written description of the commercial activity: chartering and operation of offshore platform support ships (ISIC 5222 / NAICS 483211)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The activity descriptor must match the Marine Department licence granted for offshore supply vessel operation; a mismatch between the declared ISIC code and the Cargo/Vessel licence records signals deliberate misdescription; the IRD cross-checks the business code with the vessel registry and third-party information from the Hong Kong Shipping Gazette

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Basis period (from MM-DD-YYYY to MM-DD-YYYY) and the annual accounting date, typically 31 December aligned with the PRC parent's statutory accounts
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The basis period must be a uniform 12-month period; any change to the accounting date requires IRD consent under IRO s.18E; a non-resident partnership must not include pre-commencement charter hire or post-balance-sheet bareboat hire in the wrong year to inflate an offshore loss position; such manipulation invites reassessment and treble tax penalties

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating profit or loss per the internally prepared or audited financial statements, comprising time-charter hire, bareboat charter income, voyage charter revenue, crew manning fees, demurrage and ancillary maritime service income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Where the partnership asserts an offshore claim, only profits sourced outside Hong Kong may be excluded; the partnership must attach a detailed schedule showing the charter contracts, the vessel utilisation log, the place of negotiation, the place of crew employment and the invoicing destination; excluding Hong Kong-sourced brokerage or consultancy income from this box constitutes a false return under IRO s.82 and exposes the preparer to criminal prosecution

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses disallowed under IRO s.17, including capitalised dry-dock and vessel repair costs, fines and penalties, private expenses, unsupported crew payroll, entertainment over statutory ceilings and any bribes or facilitation payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must add back 100% of vessel acquisition or major capital improvement costs that were wrongly expensed; recharged general and administrative expenses from the PRC parent must satisfy the arm's-length principle of Division 16D; royalties paid to the PRC parent for vessel management or brand intangibles must be amortised strictly under s.16(1)(f) and supported by a transfer pricing benchmarking study

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 (Deductible expenses not charged in accounts)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions not reflected in the profit and loss account, including statutory depreciation allowances on vessels (IRO s.16F), industrial building allowances, marine insurance premiums, port and registry dues, survey fees and PRC withholding taxes borne on qualifying cross-border interest
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A related-party vessel financing interest charge is deductible only at an arm's-length rate and requires contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation under DIPN 59; where the related-party interest or charter fee exceeds HK$5,000,000 a Local File must be prepared; a deduction for deemed charter fees paid to an unregistered offshore ship lessor with no commercial substance will be disallowed and recharacterised as a distribution

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of adjusted assessable profits after applying Box 5 and Box 6 adjustments, before loss set-off, with a schedule showing the amount of profits claimed as sourced outside Hong Kong
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The IRD applies the totality of facts test under DIPN 21 and DIPN 58; for offshore vessel chartering the partnership must evidence that the charter negotiations were concluded overseas by foreign brokers, the vessel performed its employment wholly on the high seas or within PRC offshore oilfield territorial waters managed from a non-HK operational base, and all hire was collected outside Hong Kong; an apportionment formula based on voyage days inside and outside Hong Kong may be accepted where the operations are mixed

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partnership tax losses utilised against current assessable profits and loss carryforward election limited to the adopted 5-year statutory limit
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident partner may only set off the partnership loss against partnership profits from the same trade; artificially migrating losses from the PRC parent through reverse invoicing or transfer-priced charter rental is a listed abuse; the IRD will reject the carryforward where the loss arises from non-arm's-length payments to a connected HK shell entity

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 9 (Two-tiered tax computation and partner distribution schedule)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of assessable profits or loss among all partners and computation of Hong Kong profits tax at 7.5% on the first HK$2,000,000 of partnership assessable profits and 15% on the excess, apportioned according to each partner's profit-share ratio
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The IRD assesses each partner separately on its partnership share; a PRC corporate partner must apply for foreign tax credit relief in China and may not claim Hong Kong personal allowances; the distribution schedule must exactly match the partnership agreement registered with the Hong Kong Business Registration Office and any Limited Partnership Fund (Cap. 637) certificate

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 10 (Offshore claim declaration and DTA relief)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration that all or part of the assessable profits are sourced outside Hong Kong, election of treaty relief for non-resident partners, certification of the foreign tax credit and confirmation of beneficial ownership of the income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The offshore claim must be accompanied by the charter party contracts with the PRC national oil company, the vessel operating log, bank statements showing remittance from outside Hong Kong, crew employment contracts and P&I insurance certificates; a knowingly false offshore claim is a criminal offence under IRO s.82(1) carrying a fine of up to HK$50,000, treble tax and imprisonment up to 3 years (and up to 10 years under s.82A for grave tax fraud); the IRD Offshore Claim audit team applies heightened evidentiary standards to vessel chartering operations

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of Form BIR52: fine of up to HK$10,000 under IRO s.80(1A) plus three times the amount of tax undercharged; continuing daily default penalties may be imposed for failure to comply with an IRD notice; late payment surcharges under s.71A: 5% where tax remains unpaid 14 days after the due date and a further 5% (cumulative 10%) after six months; fraudulent or negligent returns: conviction on indictment under s.82A attracts a fine of up to HK$50,000 plus treble tax and imprisonment up to 10 years; failure to keep sufficient records for 7 years under s.51C attracts a fine of up to HK$100,000 and imprisonment up to 2 years
